Specific heat capacity.formal: The amount of energy required to raise the temperature of one kilogram of a substance by one degree Celsius.
Specific heat capacity.example: Water: 4200 J/kg °C. So 1 kg of water needs 4200 J to warm up by 1 °C.

commands.means: Give a short answer. No explanation needed.

commands.means: Give reasons. Link each point with 'because' or 'so', and use the question's context.
commands.example: Explain why the gas pressure increases when it is heated.
commands.good: The particles move faster, so they hit the walls more often and with more force, so the pressure increases.

commands.means: Give a similarity AND a difference, talking about both things.
commands.good: Both transfer energy. Transverse waves oscillate at right angles to the direction of travel; longitudinal waves oscillate parallel to it.

commands.means: Use the information given to weigh up points for and against, then give a judgement with a reason.
commands.example: Evaluate using wind turbines to supply a town.
commands.good: Renewable and no CO₂ while running, but unreliable when it isn't windy. Good alongside a reliable supply, because…

commands.means: Apply what you know to a new situation. More than one answer can be right.
